thread:
Alex Kim: Quick sync — I'm drafting the PRD for per-tenant rate-sculpting + metering semantics. Need agreement on scope, acceptance criteria, and a safe rollout plan.
Mira Patel: high level ok. can you call out billing signals we need? meters vs charges? :thinking:
Alex Kim: want two parallel surfaces: (1) runtime enforcement (rate limits, queuing, 429 behavior), (2) billing meter (consumed tokens/requests + any burst credits consumed). Both must map to UI and API headers.
Sam Choi: +1. Also need to handle per-model overrides (eg. small model ops vs large model ops). edge case: tenant has reserved capacity -> limits should be bypassed or routed to dedicated pool?
Alex Kim: good call. proposal: reserved capacity tenants get a separate quota namespace (no runtime throttling) but still appear in metering. non-reserved tenants use sculpted limits.
Jen Ramos: can you paste the proposed config snippet so infra can review?
Alex Kim: sure — rough sketch:
```
# proposed rate profile object
profile {
  id: "per_tenant_standard"
  default_rate: 600 requests/min
  burst_capacity: 1200 tokens (refill over 60s)
  per_model_overrides: {
    "gpt-small": 1200 r/min,
    "gpt-xlarge": 120 r/min
  }
  reserved_capacity_behavior: "separate_namespace" # options: separate_namespace | fallback_queue
}
```
Mira Patel: nit: "burst_capacity" should be measured in request tokens vs requests. clarify units in PRD. Also acceptance criteria should include observability hooks (token-level meter, UI usage summary) and billing reconciliation tests.
Sam Choi: runtime behavior edgecases:
- If a tenant consumes burst and exceeds burst, do we 429 or queue?
- If multiple tenants spike, do we auto-scale or degrade SLA?
- How to handle long-running streaming requests that hold KV cache?
Alex Kim: initial plan: for non-reserved tenants, we do immediate 429 on exceeding sustained window, allow short burst up to burst_capacity, and provide a best-effort queue only for paid tier with soft-SLO. streaming requests count against token budget; we recommend per-stream soft checks.
Jen Ramos: acceptance criteria (draft):
- API supports X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining / X-RateLimit-Reset headers per tenant.
- Billing meter emits per-tenant per-model token counts to billing pipeline within 5min of end-of-request.
- UI shows current rate tier + recent spikes + estimated time-to-reset.
- Rollout plan: beta to 10 pilot tenants, canary to 100 tenants, full rollout gated by <1% 429 increase and billing reconciliation stable.
Mira Patel: add: PRD must call out error semantics for SDKs and recommend client retry policies (exponential backoff, jitter).
Sam Choi: edge case: tenants with a mix of reserved and hosted models that share the same org_id. Need mapping rules.
Alex Kim: we will add mapping table in PRD: model->execution pool mapping; org-level override rules; explicit opt-in for shared behavior.
deploy-bot: deploy job #4582 started for branch feat/rate-sculpting (ci: 1/3 checks).
Jen Ramos: next steps: Alex to convert this thread into PRD skeleton (requirements + acceptance criteria + rollout) by EOD Thu. Mira to add billing reconciliation tests. Sam to write infra RFC for "separate_namespace" behavior. I'll schedule a 30min sync Fri.
Alex Kim: sgtm, will post PRD link here when ready. :thumbsup:
Mira Patel: thanks — please call out backwards compatibility for existing API consumers (headers optional until GA).
Alex Kim: noted. tagging follow-ups: @Mira Patel for billing tests, @Sam Choi for infra RFC, @Jen Ramos for rollout.
Jen Ramos: perfect — ping me if any product tradeoffs need prioritization.
